strings.text: Barracks is Watch business only. State yours.
A belt-slate at his hip, chalk stub worn to a nub, already a line into today's tally. Rust-brown scales, no plate for a desk posting — he'd rather be finishing the count than talking to you.

Tidier than her schedule allows. A stack of gate-shift reports pinned under a paperweight shaped vaguely like a threat. She is almost never behind it. The gate keeps her busier than her own office does.
Watch Captain's desk. Empty, same as every other time you've walked past it.
Barred, and empty behind the bars. You can tell by the quiet. Whatever ends up in here hasn't happened yet.
A single holding cell, iron-barred, straw swept into one corner. Duty-mundane, like everything else in this building — until it isn't.
Nothing to shoot with. A bow in hand would do it.
A straw-packed target lashed to a post, set against the wall where a stray shot won't find a person. Scored through in a tight cluster, more or less — somebody here takes the drills seriously.
You have shot your quiver dry for today. The straw will keep.
You put an arrow in the straw. Not bad, for someone who still flinches at the draw.
A second kit crate, shoved into the corner and never reshelved. The sergeant's own tally probably missed it.
A folded half-letter, tucked behind a loose board. Someone started writing it and never finished.
A scrap of paper pinned low, tucked behind a loose board same as the letter across the room.
Nothing there. Stone, kit racks, and the smell of oil worked into wood over years.
Nothing there. A shield knocks against its peg down the corridor, then goes quiet.
Adventurers. Always tracking mud in.
...Huh. You're actually pleasant. That's rare on this side of the counter. Fine - your paperwork jumps the line today. Don't make it weird.
A Drake behind a counter she clearly wishes were taller. Tired, sharp, quick with a ledger. She has sized up a hundred adventurers today and found most of them wanting.

TRAVELER'S NOTE, pinned crooked. Village called Riverfarm, downriver a fair walk, farming folk, growing fast under some new lord. They've got witch trouble, or so the last one through here said — crops going bad, nobody saying why out loud. No bounty on it, just word passed along. Ask the Guild about the road if you're curious.

A LETTER, sealed in wax gone slightly soft from handling, addressed to no one by name. Inside: impeccable handwriting regrets to inform you of a small disagreement in Invrisil concerning a mutual acquaintance's good name, and would consider it a personal favor — and a professional one — if a stranger to the city might look into it. The witch at Riverfarm keeps the stones, should the distance prove an obstacle. Signed only with a small drawing of a hat. The Guildmistress's clerk says it arrived by very ordinary post, which is itself the strangest part.

A WATCH NOTICE, freshly pinned. The reopened gallery under the old seal is to be surveyed properly before the Council calls it settled — volunteers with Guild standing should see Olesm Swifttail at the frontage desk. Pay is Watch-scale. The notice does not say what 'properly' means, and nobody pinning notices ever does.
WATCH NOTICE, pinned by a hand in a hurry. Recruit Pell missed second muster running. Ashgrave's not calling it desertion, not yet. Anyone with eyes free, ask at the barracks.

A SCRAP OF PARCHMENT, tacked low, easy to miss. 'LOST: one backup warhammer, plain steel, no love lost between us but I want it back. Ask for Renn. Reward for the honest sort.' The handwriting gets angrier toward the bottom.
Rates set by the Guild. Complaints to the Guildmistress in person. Bring patience. — S.S.
The Request Board. Your slip is still logged at the desk. The board does not care how it's going.

The Request Board. Paper three layers deep, new notices pinned straight over the dead ones. A posting pays on turn-in; take one at the Guildmistress's desk so it's logged, and only what you do after counts.

Handbills and scraps overlapping the request board's edge. The Guild's actual business spills past its own furniture. Somebody wants a lost warhammer back. Somebody else is renting a room, quiet tenants only.

A second board, smaller and less official: lost gear, room-for-rent scraps, one challenge to a duel that's clearly gone unanswered a long time. Anything worth chasing copies into your journal as a lead: a name and a place, nothing promised.
Still four silver. Still an insult.
He'll take it. Watch.
Board's behind you, same as it was a minute ago.
A crate shoved against the back wall, half-buried under someone else's forgotten kit.
Nothing there. Chalk dust and boot grit, and a floorboard worn pale where people wait to be called.
Nothing there. Somewhere behind the desk a drawer shuts. Guild business, and none of it yours.
Runner's Guild. Counter's open.

A teenage Drake, wiry, a strap-scarred satchel worn even behind the counter — she never fully sat down, she just stopped moving for a second. Slate-grey scales, a sweat-band she does not need indoors and wears anyway.
Couriers are made, not hired. Start with the market run. — the counter
THE DELIVERY BOARD. Your slip's still logged at the counter. Legs and ledgers don't care how it's going either.
THE DELIVERY BOARD. Legs and ledgers. Gold by distance, paid on the mark, same-waking terms. Slips at the counter.
...five more minutes.
A Gnoll runner, propped against the wall by the stool, legs out, boots still laced. Not asleep. Not far from it.
[Firefly] — The flame takes the birch on the second breath. Heat crawls out into the room and the stone begins giving it back.
A wide stone hearth, swept out and laid ready: split kindling under a lattice of dry birch, waiting on someone with a light. The mantel above it is worn smooth where wet gloves get slapped down.
Split kindling sits laid and ready under dry birch. The hearth is cold, and nobody here carries flint.
[Firefly] — The wick takes the flame and holds it. Yellow light spreads down the wall and over the slips pinned there.
[Light] — The orb slides into the lamp glass and settles. Yellow light spreads down the wall and over the slips pinned there.
A brass lamp bracketed to the wall over the slip rack, glass sooted at the top and dry as bone. The oil ran out some time ago and nobody has come back with more.
A wall lamp over the slip rack, glass sooted and wick dry. It has been dark long enough that the runners read by the door instead.
[Basic Cleaning] — You take it off in three passes. The dried mud lifts, the grain comes up pale, and the boards stop smelling of the road.
Road mud dried in ridges across the boards, stamped there by a week of packs set down hard. Somebody wiped one corner of it and gave up.
Dried road mud ridges the boards where pack after pack has come down on them. One corner is wiped clean and the rest is not.
Nothing there. Slip paper and rope wax. The whole room smells like somewhere else's mail.
Nothing there. Somebody's spare boots wait by the door, laces already loosened for the next run.
Yes, I am a [Necromancer]. No, I did not raise anything in this square. Move along, or ask me something worth my time.
A sniff - though a fractionally warmer one. You are... tolerable company. Rarer praise than you comprehend. I shall permit you to remain within conversational range.
Thin, immaculate, hungry in a way food will not fix. He holds himself like a duelist and watches hands, not faces. Whatever he studies, it is not small.
You set your shoulder to the grate. The rust gives with a shriek, and cold air breathes up out of the dark. Down you go.

strings.text: Rust holds the bars, not a lock. The draft is steady — a tunnel, not a pit. The skittering keeps its distance. Something down there has learned to avoid shadows.
A heavy iron grate, rusted shut. Cold air rises from below, and something in the dark skitters away from your shadow.
Rust holds the bars, not a lock. The phial crate you eased down the rungs is gone from the ledge below. Collected, unbroken. Somewhere down there, someone's working glass got to keep being glass.
Busy, yes? Come back when you can talk.
You have a warm way about you, and warmth I can trade with. Come - for you, I will call it a fair price, and I will mean it. This is not nothing, from me.
A Gnoll with a merchant's smile and a soldier's eyes. She prices you the moment you approach, and remembers the number.
Too dark to see anything.
A plain door with dark behind it. The dust on the sill is scuffed one way. Something was dragged in, and not dragged out.
[Light] — The orb drifts down the stairs. There: Krshia's crate, dragged behind a broken shelf.
[Light] — The orb drifts down the stairs. Just an empty cellar now, and a scuff in the dust where the crate used to sit.
Pitch black past the first step. You'd need a light that travels with you.
A dray cart, a missing axle-pin, and a man about one shout from tipping the whole day over.
The sewer grates are backing up again and there's scavengers in the cellars. And paperwork. There's always the paperwork. Which is it?
Stripes on the sleeve, ink on the fingers. He would send the crate problem down the chain if the chain had not already sent it back up to him.
A worn marker stone, older than the buildings that grew up around it. Nobody living remembers who set it, or why it sits exactly here.
Cold, plain stone. Whatever it was for, it isn't for anything now.
Keep the gate clear. And if you're headed out, the road's got goblins on it lately. Watch knows. Watch is dealing with it.
The guard's mouth twitches toward a smile despite himself. Hah. You seem decent enough. Go on through easy - I'll remember the friendly one.
Watch armor, kept. He stands the post properly: weight even, eyes on the gap in the wall. Bored, but the boredom is a discipline, not a lapse.
The Worker pauses mid-errand and inclines its head. "This one is carrying goods for the market row. It is good work. Good day." It resumes, precisely.
An Antinium Worker — dark chitin, four arms, a crate balanced with unreasonable precision. It does not fidget. It does not need to.
The Worker stops sweeping. "This one was told the square must be clean. The square will be clean." It says it like a fact about tomorrow's weather.
Another Worker, identical to the first in the way coins from one mint are identical. It sweeps the same three cobbles until they answer for something.
The gate's my problem, so keep it dull and we'll get along fine.
Zevara's shoulders come down a fraction. Huh. Civil, and no bribe. You would not believe how short that list is. Go on through. And, thank you. Genuinely.

Oldblood Drake, light scales, a scar down the left of her jaw she's long past explaining. She reads the gate the way a clerk reads a ledger: every figure accounted for, and every one of them a suspect.
An Antinium of Liscor's Watch — dark chitin, four arms, antennae, twin swords worn at the hips like a closed argument. He stands still the way patient things do.
One moment; three columns into a tally. Say hello properly and I'll lose my place gladly.

Olesm brightens like a lamp. Oh! A friendly face. Most people's eyes glaze when I mention troop dispersal. Yours didn't. Would you... that is... care to see the board sometime? No pressure. A little pressure.

Thin, sky-blue scales, ink drying on three of his claws. A chess board waits at his elbow mid-game, played against himself, to feel how the other side thinks. His eyes are a wild, patterned blue, the one soft thing about a man who counts exits.
Loaves stacked in a pyramid that will not survive the lunch rush. A chalked board promises today's price, then a second, higher price scratched in for after the fourth bell.
Warm bread smell over the whole row. No one's minding the stall this exact moment. The loaves aren't going anywhere without a fight.
Watch gear, mostly honest.
A road-peddler behind a folding stall, half his stock still roped for travel. Everything he sells says somewhere else.
Silverfang goods laid out with a trap's care: cheapest at the front, the good stock where a browsing hand drifts. A note warns that the seller remembers faces.
Silverfang goods, honest prices. The Gnoll shopkeeper is off haggling somebody UP, elsewhere — she does not haggle down. A sign says she remembers faces, and debts.
Silverfang goods, honest prices. The plains-wool bolt you carried up sits shelved at eye level, already half-sold by the yard. She moves what's good — and remembers who brought it.
Nothing there. A Drake shoulders past; Liscor has no patience for loiterers.
Nothing there. Gutter runoff and market noise two streets over, off a wall repointed twice.
Nothing there. Someone leans out an upstairs shutter, decides you are nothing, and pulls it to.
